data.title: 'The End of Oak Street' survives dinosaur fatigue with family drama
data.description: The poorly received 2025 film ‘Jurassic World Rebirth’ made a meta-commentary on how people no longer care about dinosaurs. The claim is reasonable, considering the dinosaur thriller genre has been on the silver screen for over 30 years, since the original Jurassic Park in 1993. Surprisingly, ‘ The End of Oak Street ’ (2026) manages a fun and fresh take on the genre, balancing intimate family drama with the big idea of a suburban street thrust into a prehistoric world.

data.title: Player: Little man with a big influence
data.description: The Piccadilly World Matchplay was held each year at Wentworth and l went to watch whenever l possibly could, which meant occasionally skipping school. This was the first time l saw Gary Player play on the course which he dominated, as he won the event five times. He was a small man in stature, but this was made up for by his determination to be one of the best who practised like a man possessed. His 'never give up' attitude was infuriating for the vast majority of his opponents -- not least for Tony Lema in 1965 who lost against Player when he was 7-up at one stage in his match with the little man.
